coverNote: Start with “The short version” and Part 4, which splits the work into packages with an owner slot on each. Parts 2 and 3 are the reference behind them. Every number carries a tag that says how sure we are of it.
howMade: **How this was compiled.** I followed our orchestration design. Sonnet agents first extracted every idea, bottleneck and term from the sources without judging them, each record with a citation in the form `path:line — quote`. I merged duplicates and sorted the records into themes and work packages. Fresh-context Opus agents then checked 469 [M] idea records and every number in the narrative against the sources; 268 [M] idea records and 11 [M] narrative claims were corrected or tightened, and the corrected text is what is printed here. Where the record does not know something, this compile says so. Throughout, “I” is me and “we” is the team.
heatShows: Review and fix rounds draw the most ideas (143 [M]), then the orchestrator and lanes (105 [M]). Memory has the most open bottlenecks for its ideas: 22 [M] of its 23 are open, against 46 [M] ideas, so that is where most of the new work is.
